mainTopic: Hard learning and its remedies, prayer and rain, faith, and strict judgment of the righteous: a chain of אגדות on פסוקים
overview: This amud is a chain of אגדה teachings built on פסוקים. It opens with two readings of 'אם קהה הברזל' (קהלת 10:10), about learning that feels hard as iron. ריש לקיש blames a student's disorganized משנה and says the fix is more study, backed up by the review habits of ריש לקיש and רב אדא בר אהבה. רבא blames a teacher who does not show a friendly face, and says the fix is friends who speak up for the student. רבי אמי then reads the next פסוק about the snake and the charmer as being about rain: the heavens hold back rain when no one prays quietly and properly. The remedy is to go to someone who knows how to pray, and if that fails, to the חסיד of the generation. The גמרא also warns that pride after an answered prayer, and rivalry between scholars, bring anger into the world. Further teachings follow: the snake and לשון הרע, sincere prayer for a יחיד versus a ציבור, rain in the merit of בעלי אמנה, and exact judgment for those who are exacting with themselves. The amud ends with ריש לקיש comparing closed heavens to a woman in labor who cannot give birth, a teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: hard learning comes from unorganized basics
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his statement: when learning feels hard as iron, the cause is that the student's משנה is not organized in his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: (If you see a student) whose learning is as hard for him as iron, it is because his משנה is not organized for him, as the פסוק says: 'and he did not sharpen the face.'
steps.whatsHappening: The text opens in the middle of ריש לקיש's statement, which began on the previous daf. He explains why some students find learning as hard as iron.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads the פסוק's word פנים as the 'surface,' meaning the basic text of the משנה. He reads קלקל as 'spoiled.' If the basics are messy, everything built on top of them will feel hard.

keyTerms.meaning: as hard for him as iron, very difficult to grasp
his משנה, the basic text he learned

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new statement. The opening words 'If you see a student' and ריש לקיש's name appear on the previous daf.

phrases.english: whose learning is as hard for him as iron —
phrases.notes: This continues ריש לקיש's words from the previous daf: 'If you see a student...'

phrases.english: it is because of his משנה
which is not organized for him,
as it is said: 'and he did not sharpen the face.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:10. Here 'face' is read as the surface, meaning the basic text.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁתַּלְמוּדוֹ קָשֶׁה עָלָיו כַּבַּרְזֶל בִּשְׁבִיל מִשְׁנָתוֹ שֶׁאֵינָהּ סְדוּרָה עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's statement that began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning feels hard as iron when the student's basic משנה is not well organized.

steps.title: What is the fix?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what such a student should do.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: how can this student fix his problem?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know the cause of the problem from step 1. The question moves the discussion from diagnosis to treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: what is his remedy / what can fix it

phrases.english: What is his remedy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the solution to the problem described in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a student whose basics are disorganized can fix his learning.

steps.title: Study more, and better yet, organize from the start
steps.stepSummary: The fix is to spend more time studying, as the פסוק says. Having the משנה organized from the beginning is even better.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should spend more time sitting and learning, as it says: 'then he must increase strength,' and 'the advantage of preparing is wisdom.' All the more so if his משנה is organized for him from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question using the rest of the same פסוק. The answer is extra effort, though preparing properly from the beginning is best.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Increase strength' is read as putting in more hours of study. The end of the פסוק, 'the advantage of preparing is wisdom,' teaches that getting it organized from the start saves all that extra effort.

keyTerms.meaning: he should spend more time sitting and studying

phrases.english: He should increase his sitting (in study),
as it is said: 'then he must increase strength,'
'and the advantage of preparing is wisdom.'
All the more so if his משנה
is organized for him from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: יַרְבֶּה בִּישִׁיבָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַחֲיָלִים יְגַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: More study time fixes the problem, and organized learning from the start is better still.

steps.title: Great scholars who reviewed many times before class
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reviewed his learning 40 times before going to רבי יוחנן. רב אדא בר אהבה reviewed 24 times before going to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like ריש לקיש, who would review his learning forty times, matching the forty days the תורה was given, and then go in to רבי יוחנן. רב אדא בר אהבה would review his learning twenty-four times, matching תורה, נביאים and כתובים, and then go in to רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives real examples of students who organized their learning before going to their teachers. They show the advice of step 3 in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both scholars reviewed many times before learning with their teacher, so their basics were set 'from the start.' Each number has meaning: 40 matches the days משה spent receiving the תורה, and 24 matches the books of תנ"ך.

keyTerms.meaning: reviewed / set in order his learning

steps.whatToRemember: Reviewing your learning many times before class, as ריש לקיש and רב אדא בר אהבה did, is the ideal way to keep learning from becoming 'hard as iron.'

phrases.english: Like this practice of Reish Lakish:
he would review his learning
forty times,
corresponding to the forty days in which the Torah was given,
and then go in before Rabbi Yochanan.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מְסַדַּר מַתְנִיתֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava would review his learning
twenty-four times,
corresponding to Torah, Prophets, and Writings,
and then go in before Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲוָה מְסַדַּר מַתְנִיתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows examples of the advice given in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That organizing your learning from the start is the ideal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The review habits of ריש לקיש and רב אדא בר אהבה.

steps.title: רבא: the teacher's unfriendly face is the cause
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the same פסוק differently: learning becomes hard when the teacher does not show the student a friendly face.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If you see a student whose learning is as hard for him as iron, it is because of his teacher, who does not show him a friendly face, as the פסוק says: 'and he did not sharpen the face.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second explanation of the same פסוק. In his reading the problem lies with the teacher, not the student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, פנים meant the 'surface' of the משנה. For רבא, פנים means the teacher's face, his expression toward the student. A stern, unwelcoming teacher makes learning feel hard.

keyTerms.meaning: shows him a friendly, welcoming face

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing that ריש לקיש is wrong about the facts. He reads the word פנים in the same פסוק a different way, so he points to a different cause.
steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק gives two causes for hard learning: disorganized basics (ריש לקיש) or an unfriendly teacher (רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:
If you see a student
whose learning is as hard for him as iron —
it is because of his teacher
who does not show him a friendly face,
as it is said: 'and he did not sharpen the face.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, but now 'face' means the teacher's expression.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אִם רָאִיתָ תַּלְמִיד שֶׁתַּלְמוּדוֹ קָשֶׁה עָלָיו כַּבַּרְזֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the פסוק explained by ריש לקיש in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning feels hard as iron when the teacher does not show the student a friendly face.

steps.title: The fix: bring friends to speak up for you
steps.stepSummary: The student whose teacher is unfriendly to him should get many friends to speak up for him. It is even better if he behaves properly before his teacher from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: What can this student do? He should get many friends to speak to the teacher for him, as the פסוק says, 'he must add strength.' But 'wisdom makes things right,' so it is even better if he behaved properly before his teacher from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the student from step 5 can do when his teacher does not show him a friendly face, and it answers right away: bring friends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This copies the pattern of steps 2 and 3. There the fix was to study more, and better still to have the משנה organized from the start. Here the fix is friends who speak up for him, and better still is to have behaved properly before his teacher from the start. The word חילים, 'strength,' is also read as a group of people backing him up.

keyTerms.meaning: He should get many friends to speak up for him
'He must add strength.' Here it is read as adding a group of supporters

steps.whatToRemember: Both fixes in this part of the sugya follow the same pattern: there is a way to repair the problem, but preventing it from the start is better.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
phrases.notes: This is the student from step 5, whose teacher does not show him a friendly face.

phrases.english: He should increase friends on his behalf,
phrases.notes: Friends who go to the teacher and put in a good word for him.

phrases.english: as it says: "And he must add strength,"
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:10. חילים can also mean troops, so here it means a group of people backing him.

phrases.english: "but wisdom has the advantage of making things right."
All the more so if his deeds were made proper
before his teacher from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי תקנתיה — ירבה עליו רעים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fix for the problem רבא described in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What can a student do when his teacher is not friendly to him?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Get many friends to speak up for him. It is better still to have behaved properly before his teacher from the start.

steps.title: No rain because no one prays quietly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי reads the פסוק about a snake and a charmer as talking about rain. When the heavens are 'rusted like copper' and hold back rain, it is because the generation has no one who prays quietly and properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: What does the פסוק mean, 'If the snake bites without a charm, then the charmer has no advantage'? If you see a generation whose heavens are rusted like copper and do not bring down dew and rain, it is because there are no people in that generation who pray quietly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of the מסכת, rain. רבי אמי gives a new reading of a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי builds on similar-sounding words. ישך, 'bites,' sounds like משתכין, 'rusted.' נחש, 'snake,' sounds like נחשת, 'copper.' לחש, 'charm,' is read as a quiet prayer. So the פסוק becomes: the heavens are rusted shut because no one is praying quietly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rusted or corroded, so the heavens are 'stuck' shut
'Master of the tongue.' Someone skilled with words, the charmer

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about real snakes or magic charms. רבי אמי uses the sound of the words to read the whole פסוק as being about prayer and rain.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
What is meant by that which is written:
"If the snake bites without a charm,"
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:11

phrases.english: "then the master of the tongue has no advantage"?
If you see a generation
whose heavens are rusted like copper,
phrases.notes: Wordplay: ישך sounds like משתכין, and נחש sounds like נחשת.

phrases.english: so they do not bring down dew and rain,
it is because people who whisper quiet prayers
are missing from the generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר רבי אמי מאי דכתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the learning topic and goes back to rain, the main subject of the מסכת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When rain is held back, the reason is that the generation has no one who knows how to pray quietly and properly.

steps.title: The fix: go to someone who knows how to pray
steps.stepSummary: The generation should go to a person who knows how to pray properly, as the פסוק says 'his friend speaks up for him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What can they do? They should go to someone who knows how to pray, as it is written, 'His friend speaks up for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how a generation without rain can fix its problem, and answers that they should go to a person who knows how to pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof פסוק is read as 'his friend tells about him.' Someone else speaks up on his behalf. This is the same idea as the friends in step 6: when you cannot get through yourself, bring someone who can.

keyTerms.meaning: To whisper, which here means to pray quietly and properly

phrases.english: What is their remedy?
They should go to someone who knows how to whisper his prayers,
as it is written: "His friend speaks up for him."
phrases.notes: איוב 36:33. The גמרא reads רעו as 'his friend,' someone who prays on his behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי תקנתן — ילכו אצל מי שיודע ללחוש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fix for the problem described in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What can a generation without rain do?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Go to someone who knows how to pray properly.

steps.title: The one who can pray but does not
steps.stepSummary: The end of the קהלת פסוק is about a person who knows how to pray but does not do it. His skill does him no good.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the master of the tongue has no advantage': someone who can pray properly but does not, what good does it do him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and explains the last words of the קהלת פסוק from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 used the first half of the פסוק. Now the second half, 'no advantage to the master of the tongue,' is applied to a person who knows how to pray but does not bother. His ability is useless if he does not use it.

phrases.english: "And the master of the tongue has no advantage":
phrases.notes: Back to the end of the קהלת פסוק from step 7.

phrases.english: someone who is able to whisper his prayers
but does not whisper them,
what benefit does he have?

steps.triggerLanguage: ואין יתרון לבעל הלשון ומי שאפשר לו ללחוש ואינו לוחש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes reading the קהלת פסוק that step 7 started.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who knows how to pray but does not do it gets no benefit from his skill.

steps.title: If prayer fails, go to the חסיד of the generation
steps.stepSummary: If someone prayed and was not answered, he should go to the most pious person of the generation, who will pray hard for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he prayed and was not answered, what can he do? He should go to the חסיד of the generation, who will pray a lot for him, as it says, 'And He commanded it because of the one who pleads.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a harder version of the question: what if he did pray and still got no answer? It answers that he should go to the חסיד of the generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the next level up. First you need someone who knows how to pray (step 8). If that is not enough, you go to the most pious person, whose prayer has extra power. The proof is the פסוק right before the one in step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: The most pious person of the generation

phrases.english: And if he whispered his prayers and was not answered,
what is his remedy?
He should go to the pious man of the generation,
and he will pray a great deal for him,
as it says: "And He commanded it because of the one who pleads."
phrases.notes: איוב 36:32, the פסוק just before the one in step 8.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואם לחש ולא נענה מאי תקנתיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the fix from step 8 one level further, for when prayer did not work.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What can someone do if he prayed and was not answered?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Go to the חסיד of the generation, who will pray a great deal for him.

steps.title: Proof that פגיעה means prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from ירמיהו that the word פגיעה means prayer, so the פסוק in איוב really is about prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And פגיעה means only prayer, as it says: 'And you, do not pray for this people, do not raise a cry or prayer for them, and do not plead with Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its reading of מפגיע in step 10 by showing that the same word is used for prayer in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10's proof only works if מפגיע means praying. In ירמיהו, 'do not plead with Me' (אל תפגע בי) appears right next to 'do not pray,' which shows that פגיעה is a kind of prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: Pleading. Here it is shown to mean prayer
'Means nothing other than,' a formula for defining a word

steps.whatToRemember: The order of remedies for no rain: a person who knows how to pray, and if that fails, the חסיד of the generation, who prays a great deal.

phrases.english: And pleading means nothing other than prayer,
as it says: "And you, do not pray
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 7:16

phrases.english: for this people,
and do not lift up a cry or prayer for them,
and do not plead with Me."

steps.triggerLanguage: ואין פגיעה אלא תפילה שנאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the word meaning that step 10's proof depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That מפגיע in the פסוק in איוב refers to prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 7:16, where 'do not plead with Me' appears together with 'do not pray.'

steps.title: Becoming proud after a successful prayer brings anger
steps.stepSummary: If someone prayed quietly and was answered, and then became proud, he brings anger into the world. The source is 'מקנה אף על עולה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he whispered his prayer and it worked, and then he becomes proud of himself, he brings anger into the world. As the פסוק says: 'Anger is gained by one who lifts himself up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the איוב passage about prayer. It now explains the second half of איוב 36:33, the same פסוק quoted in step 8, and warns about the person whose prayer was answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps praised the person who prays quietly and properly. Here the same person can still ruin it: if success makes him proud, he brings anger instead of blessing. The words 'מקנה אף על עולה' are read as 'anger is acquired by one who raises himself up.'

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes proud; thinks highly of himself
One who rises up, here meaning one who lifts himself up in pride

steps.confusionAlert: In איוב the simple meaning of the words is about cattle and a rising storm. The גמרא is reading the same words in a new way as a lesson about pride.

phrases.english: And if he whispered his prayer and it succeeded for him,
and he becomes proud because of it,
he brings anger into the world,
as it says: 'Anger is gained by one who lifts himself up.'
phrases.notes: איוב 36:33

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם לָחַשׁ וְעָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the איוב passage. It reads the second half of איוב 36:33, the פסוק quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One whose prayer is answered and who then becomes proud brings anger into the world.

steps.title: Two scholars who are not kind to each other stir up anger
steps.stepSummary: רבא applies the same פסוק to two תלמידי חכמים in one city who do not treat each other well in their Torah discussions. They stir up anger and make it rise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Two Torah scholars who live in the same city and are not pleasant with each other in הלכה stir up anger and make it rise, as it says: 'Anger is gained by one who lifts himself up.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second reading of the same פסוק 'מקנה אף על עולה.' This time it is about scholars who argue without respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'מקנה' as coming from קנאה, jealous rivalry, and 'עולה' as making the anger rise. So the lesson moves from one proud person to two scholars whose rivalry causes Divine anger. The point is about how they treat each other, not about disagreeing in הלכה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Are not pleasant or courteous with one another
Stir up, arouse (related to קנאה, jealous anger)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the way scholars argue matters. Rivalry in Torah learning without respect can bring harm to the whole world.

phrases.english: רבא said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין בְּעִיר אַחַת
phrases.english: Two Torah scholars who live in one city
and are not pleasant with each other in הלכה,
they stir up anger and make it rise,
as it says: 'Anger is gained by one who lifts himself up.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק used in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars in one city who are not courteous with each other in הלכה stir up Divine anger.

steps.title: The animals ask the snake why it bites
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the קהלת פסוק about the snake as a lesson about לשון הרע. In the future the animals will ask the snake what it gains from biting, and the snake will answer that the slanderer gains even less.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does the פסוק 'If the snake bites without a charm, the master of the tongue has no advantage' mean? In the future all the animals will gather by the snake and say: A lion tramples and eats, a wolf tears and eats, but you, what do you get out of it? The snake will answer: 'The master of the tongue has no advantage' either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another reading of the קהלת פסוק from step 7. This time it is a story about the animals and the snake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lion and a wolf at least eat what they kill, but the snake bites and gets nothing. The snake answers by pointing to the 'בעל הלשון,' the person who speaks לשון הרע: he hurts people and gets no pleasure at all. The words that meant 'charmer' in step 7 are read here as 'master of the tongue,' the slanderer.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future time to come
Master of the tongue; here, a person who speaks לשון הרע

steps.confusionAlert: The snake is not saying he has no answer. He is turning the question around: 'Why ask me? Ask the slanderer, who gains even less than I do.'

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said: What is the meaning of what is written:
'If the snake bites without a charm,'
'then the master of the tongue has no advantage'?
phrases.notes: קהלת 10:11

phrases.english: In the future they will gather and come,
all the animals, to the snake,
and they will say to him:
A lion tramples its prey and eats it,
a wolf tears its prey and eats it,
but you, what pleasure do you get?
phrases.notes: The snake bites people but cannot eat them, so what does it gain?

phrases.english: He will say to them: 'The master of the tongue has no advantage either.'
phrases.notes: He means the person who speaks לשון הרע hurts others and gets nothing at all from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the קהלת פסוק from steps 7 and 9 and reads it in a new way, about לשון הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The slanderer is worse than the snake: he causes harm and gains no benefit at all.

steps.title: Prayer is heard only when a person puts his whole self into it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that a person's prayer is heard only if he 'places his soul in his palm,' meaning he prays with complete sincerity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: A person's prayer is heard only if he puts his soul in his hand, as it says: 'Let us lift up our heart with our hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי gives a new rule about what makes a prayer accepted. It must come with the whole heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from איכה: 'Let us lift our heart with our hands.' Lifting the hands is not enough. The heart has to go up with them. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Places his soul in his palm; prays with total sincerity

phrases.english: רבי אמי said:
A person's prayer is not heard

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מֵשִׂים נַפְשׁוֹ בְּכַפּוֹ,
phrases.english: unless he places his soul in his palm,
phrases.notes: He means the person gives over his whole heart in his raised hands as he prays.

phrases.english: as it says: 'Let us lift up our heart with our hands.'
phrases.notes: איכה 3:41

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין תְּפִלָּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם נִשְׁמַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about prayer that is not tied to the earlier פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer is heard only when it is said with full sincerity.

steps.title: שמואל's teaching shows that even insincere prayer was forgiven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי from a דרשה of שמואל. The פסוק says the people flattered ה׳ with their mouths while their hearts were not with Him, and still ה׳ is merciful and forgives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But שמואל set up a speaker for himself and taught: 'They fooled Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue, their heart was not true with Him, and they were not faithful to His covenant.' And even so: 'But He is merciful, He forgives sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אמי's rule with a פסוק in תהלים that שמואל taught in public. The next step answers this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said only a sincere prayer is heard. The פסוקים in תהלים describe people whose words were fake and whose hearts were not loyal, yet the next פסוק says ה׳ forgave them. That seems to show that even a prayer without a sincere heart can be accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the speaker who repeats the teacher's words out loud to the crowd

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אמי's rule is rejected. The next step answers this challenge by showing the two teachings are about different cases.

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אוֹקֵים שְׁמוּאֵל אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ:
phrases.english: But שמואל set up a speaker for himself and taught:
phrases.notes: An אמורא here is the person who repeated the teacher's words loudly so the whole crowd could hear.

phrases.english: 'They fooled Him with their mouth and lied to Him with their tongue,'
'their heart was not true with Him,'
'and they were not faithful to His covenant.'
And even so,
'But He is merciful, He forgives sin,' and so on!
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:38

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אוֹקֵים שְׁמוּאֵל אָמוֹרָא עֲלֵיהּ וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אמי's rule from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's rule that only a sincere prayer is heard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים in תהלים describe insincere words and disloyal hearts, yet ה׳ still forgave. So insincere prayer can also be accepted.

steps.title: Individual prayer versus community prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי אמי's demand for full sincerity applies to a יחיד, while שמואל's teaching that ה׳ forgives even insincere prayer applies to a ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here it is talking about an individual, and there it is talking about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 16 by showing that the two teachings speak about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי said prayer is heard only if it is fully sincere, but שמואל's פסוק showed ה׳ forgiving people who flattered Him with their mouths. The answer: a person praying alone needs full sincerity. When the whole community prays, ה׳ accepts the prayer even if it is lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is the standard opening of an answer that removes a contradiction.
An individual praying on his own

steps.whatToRemember: A יחיד needs a sincere heart for his prayer to be heard, but the prayer of the ציבור is accepted even when it is imperfect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows how much power there is in davening together with the community.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is talking about an individual;
phrases.notes: "Here" is רבי אמי's rule that prayer must be fully sincere.

phrases.english: there, it is talking about a community.
phrases.notes: "There" is שמואל's פסוק about ה׳ forgiving the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּיָחִיד, כָּאן בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16 against רבי אמי's teaching in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if שמואל's פסוק proved that even insincere prayer is always accepted, which would contradict רבי אמי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sincerity is required for a יחיד. A ציבור is answered even without full sincerity.

steps.title: Rain falls only because of faithful people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי teaches that rain falls only in the merit of בעלי אמנה. He learns this from the פסוק 'Truth springs out of the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Rain falls only because of faithful people, as it says: 'Truth springs out of the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי אמי, connecting rain to the merit of faithful people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two halves. When 'truth' grows from the earth, meaning people are faithful, then 'righteousness' comes down from heaven, meaning rain. Faithfulness below brings blessing from above.

keyTerms.meaning: Faithful people, people of trust and faith

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Rain does not fall
except because of faithful people,
as it is said: "Truth springs out of the earth,
phrases.notes: תהלים 85:12

phrases.english: and righteousness has looked down from heaven."
phrases.notes: He reads "righteousness from heaven" as the rain that comes down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין גְּשָׁמִים יוֹרְדִין אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל בַּעֲלֵי אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the discussion about prayer, the גמרא brings another teaching from the same speaker, רבי אמי, on a new theme: faith and rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain comes in the merit of בעלי אמנה.

steps.title: How great faith is: the lesson of the weasel and the pit
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי shows the greatness of בעלי אמנה from the story of the חולדה and the בור. If faith in a weasel and a pit had such power, faith in ה׳ surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אמי said: Come and see how great faithful people are. From where do we know this? From the weasel and the pit. If this is what happens to someone who trusted a weasel and a pit, then for someone who trusts in the הקדוש ברוך הוא, how much more so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי adds a second teaching about faithful people and proves it with a קל וחומר from a well-known story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is only hinted at here. A couple made a weasel and a pit their witnesses to a promise, and those witnesses ended up enforcing it. If trusting simple creatures and objects had such results, trusting ה׳ will have far greater results.

keyTerms.meaning: How much more so. This is the language of a קל וחומר.
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
Come and see how great
faithful people are.
From where do we know this? From the weasel and the pit.
phrases.notes: This points to a known story about a couple who made a weasel and a pit the witnesses to their promise.

phrases.english: Now if one who trusted in a weasel and a pit had this outcome,
then one who trusts in the Holy One, Blessed be He,
how much more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גְּדוֹלִים בַּעֲלֵי אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אמי's theme of בעלי אמנה with a second teaching built on a קל וחומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Faith in ה׳ has great power, learned by קל וחומר from the חולדה ובור story.

steps.title: Being exacting with yourself brings exact judgment from above
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that whoever is exacting with himself below is judged exactly from above. He uses the same פסוק of 'truth from the earth, righteousness from heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Whoever is exacting with himself below is judged exactly from above, as it says: 'Truth springs out of the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן that uses the same פסוק as רבי אמי, but reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי read the פסוק as being about rain. רבי יוחנן reads it as being about judgment. The way a person carefully judges his own actions on earth is matched by how carefully ה׳ judges him in heaven, in order to help him grow even further.

keyTerms.meaning: Being exacting with oneself, carefully acting righteously
Below, on earth / above, in heaven
He is judged in an exact, strict way

steps.confusionAlert: Being judged exactly above is not presented as a punishment for being careful. It is ה׳ holding a careful person to his own high level.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whoever is exacting with himself below,
is judged in an exact manner from above,
as it is said: "Truth springs out of the earth,
and righteousness has looked down from heaven."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַמַּצְדִּיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new teaching built on the same פסוק that רבי אמי used in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: How exacting a person is with himself below determines how exactly he is judged above.

steps.title: A second source: God's anger matches a person's fear of Him
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין, quoting רב הונא, learns רבי יוחנן's idea from a different פסוק: 'And Your wrath is according to the fear of You.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב הונא: We learn it from here: 'And Your wrath is according to the fear of You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different פסוק as the source for רבי יוחנן's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea stays the same and only the source changes. The פסוק teaches that ה׳'s strictness toward a person matches that person's level of fear of Heaven. The more a person fears ה׳, the more exactly he is judged.

keyTerms.meaning: From here. It introduces a different source for the same idea.
The fear of You, fear of Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: Both sources teach the same thing: the more careful and God-fearing a person is, the more exactly ה׳ judges him.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav Huna said:
From here: "And Your wrath is according to the fear of You."
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:11

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for רבי יוחנן's teaching in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: How strictly ה׳ judges a person matches that person's fear of Heaven, learned from 'וּכְיִרְאָתְךָ עֶבְרָתֶךָ'.

steps.title: ריש לקיש brings a third verse for exact judgment
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different פסוק as the source for the idea that ה׳ judges the righteous very exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: we learn it from here: 'You struck the one who joyfully does righteousness, those who remember You in Your ways. Behold, You were angry, and we sinned. Upon them we have stood forever, and we will be saved.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers his own פסוק for the same idea that רבי יוחנן and רב הונא taught. That idea is that people who are careful with themselves are judged carefully by ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן used 'truth from the earth.' רב הונא used 'Your wrath is according to the fear of You.' ריש לקיש reads this פסוק as saying that ה׳'s anger comes on the people who joyfully do righteousness when they sin. The more righteous a person is, the more exactly ה׳ judges him.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a different source
You struck or met. Here it means ה׳ deals strictly with someone

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: from here
phrases.notes: He's giving his own source for רבי יוחנן's idea: whoever is exacting with himself is judged exactly.

phrases.english: "You struck the one who joyfully does righteousness,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 64:4

phrases.english: those who remember You in Your ways;
behold, You were angry, and we sinned;
upon them we have stood forever, and we will be saved."

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, different פסוק for the same teaching of רבי יוחנן, after רב הונא's פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The righteous are judged strictly. ה׳'s anger comes on those who joyfully do righteousness when they sin.

steps.title: Joy in suffering brings salvation to the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the end of the same פסוק to teach that whoever accepts his suffering with joy brings salvation to the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Whoever is happy with the suffering that comes on him brings salvation to the world, as it says: 'Upon them, the world, and we will be saved.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a new lesson from the same פסוק ריש לקיש just quoted. He says that a person who accepts suffering with joy brings salvation to the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He focuses on the word 'עולם' in the פסוק. It usually means 'forever,' but he reads it as 'the world.' So the פסוק teaches that through such people, the world is saved.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is happy with his suffering
Forever, or the world. He reads it as 'world' here

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Whoever is happy with the suffering
that comes upon him
brings salvation to the world,
as it is said: "Upon them, the world, and we will be saved."
phrases.notes: In the פסוק, עולם means 'forever,' but he reads it as 'the world.' That is his whole proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק as ריש לקיש, but draws a different lesson from its last words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever accepts his suffering with joy brings salvation to the world.

steps.title: Closed heavens are like a woman in labor who cannot give birth
steps.stepSummary: Going back to rain, ריש לקיש explains that when the heavens hold back dew and rain, they are like a woman in labor pains who cannot give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: What does it mean when the פסוק says 'And He will close up the heavens'? When the heavens are closed up from bringing down dew and rain, it is like a woman who has labor pains but does not give birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of rain. ריש לקיש explains the פסוק about ה׳ 'closing' the heavens by comparing it to a woman stuck in labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the comparison is that holding back rain is not calm or peaceful. It is like the pain of a birth that is stuck. The rain is ready to come but is held back.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
What is the meaning of what is written: "And He will close up the heavens"?
phrases.notes: דברים 11:17

phrases.english: When the heavens are closed up
from bringing down dew and rain,
it is like a woman who has labor pains
and does not give birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the righteous and suffering, and goes back to the main subject of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the heavens hold back rain, they are like a woman in labor who cannot give birth.

steps.title: בר קפרא's teaching backs up the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that ריש לקיש's comparison matches another teaching he said in the name of בר קפרא: the Torah uses the word 'closing' for both rain and a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what ריש לקיש said in the name of בר קפרא: 'Closing' is said about rain, and 'closing' is said about a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports ריש לקיש's comparison with a word link from בר קפרא. This step is setting up the next move, where the גמרא will continue this teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והיינו' means 'this is the same idea as.' The same word, עצירה, is used both for the heavens holding back rain and for a woman whose womb is closed. Because the Torah uses the same word, the two cases can be compared.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as, introducing a matching teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The teaching is not finished here. The גמרא continues it on the next amud, so do not treat this line as the full conclusion.

phrases.english: And this is what Reish Lakish said
in the name of Bar Kappara:
"Closing" is said about rain,
and "closing" is said about a woman,
phrases.notes: On the next amud the גמרא goes on to show where the תורה says 'closing' about a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the comparison in step 24 with a word link taught by בר קפרא.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's comparison of closed heavens to a woman in labor
steps.raayaSupportSource: בר קפרא's teaching that the word עצירה is used for both rain and a woman
